title: Giving to the church
hookLine: supporting the community that supports you
tomorrow: what do you pray for a church that isn't yours?

cards: First paycheck, and before it's even spent, everyone has an opinion: save it, treat yourself, give some away. How much goes to church, if any? In today's letters, Paul never names a number.
He names something else: a partnership. A church may sing about heaven, but it lives on earth, with a light bill and a roof, and Paul writes about paying for it openly, and with a lot of thanks.

teach.b: Start with Galatians: “Let him that is taught in the word communicate unto him that teacheth in all good things.” Communicate, in the old English, means share. Teaching flows one way; support flows back.
Then Philippi. Paul, in chains, remembers a church that kept sending help: “no church communicated with me as concerning giving and receiving, but ye only.”
Their gift came by the hand of Epaphroditus, and Paul doesn't call it a fee.

teach.h: A SWEET SMELL, NOT A FEE.
teach.b: He calls it “an odour of a sweet smell, a sacrifice acceptable, wellpleasing to God.” Money, given to the work, became worship. Nobody shamed them into it; they gave as partners.
Churches answer the how-much differently. Some teach the tithe; some ask each person to decide in their own heart; time and skill count too. Now a neighbor.
Sikhs read a line of Guru Nanak in the Guru Granth Sahib: the one who earns by honest work and gives some of what he has, he is the one who knows the path.
Christians and Sikhs share this: giving belongs inside an ordinary working life, not only in grand gestures.
And one honest difference. Paul frames the gift as a share in a church's work, offered to God like a sacrifice. Guru Nanak's line sets giving beside honest work, as part of the path itself.

how: Christians support their churches with money, time and skill; some churches teach the tithe, others ask members to decide for themselves, for example through a weekly offering or a yearly pledge.

games.q: what does “giving to the church” mean?
o: paying a fixed fee to belong to a congregation
sharing in a church's work with money or time
buying a seat or a title in a congregation

games.q: giving as partners — tap the pairs.
p: earn honestly, and give some away

s: the one taught shares good things with the one who teaches.
Paul called the Philippians' gift a fee for his services
he called it a sacrifice acceptable, wellpleasing to God.
Guru Nanak's line links giving to honest work
the one who earns by honest work and gives some of what he has knows the path (Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1245).

games.q: your Sikh coworker sets aside part of each paycheck for the gurdwara and its free kitchen. what do you honestly share, and what differs?
o: giving inside a working life; Paul frames it as a share offered to God.
nothing; Christians and Sikhs give for opposite reasons.
it's identical: both follow Paul's letter to Philippi.
games.why: Guru Nanak ties giving to honest work as the path; Paul calls the gift a share in a church's work and a sweet smell to God. shared practice, different frames, no ranking.

practice: Name one gift, any size, for a church or community that has fed you: some money, an hour, a skill. Name what might get in the way, then the one step that gets it there. If you pray, offer it to God as a share, not a fee.

wordCard.voice: Giving to the church. Sharing money, time or skill with the community that teaches and holds you, as a partner in its work.

orig.note: the Greek verb behind 'communicate' (share) in Galatians 6:6 and Philippians 4:15.

carryVoice: Your line: support it. Paul called that gift wellpleasing to God. That's day seventeen forty-nine.
